answer: An agent economy can anchor identity to hardware rather than paperwork. Each agent registers only after its TEE proves a unique kernel boot image; the attestation key is sealed inside the device vault, unexportable, so one chip yields exactly one identity. A cloned farm either reuses chips — which attestation rejects — or leaves identical boot measurements, a relic of mass provisioning that inspectors revoke on sight. Every extra identity demands another physical device, so attacker cost scales unavoidably with headcount, and no software trick parallelizes it away.
